# Workflows

The GitHub Actions workflows of the repository.  [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) says when a contributor meets them; [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) holds the rules of changing them.  [`docs/publishing.md`](../../docs/publishing.md) covers versioning and releasing.

## The workflows

| Workflow | Runs on | Does |
|----|----|----|
| `ci.yml` | Pull requests to `main` or an `integration/*` branch, pushes to them | Calls `build.yml` and ends with the `ci` job |
| `build.yml` | Called by `ci.yml` and `publish.yml` | Jobs that start at once and need none of the others: `Lint`, the Docker-only checks; `Site`, the docfx build of the manual by `tools/build-site.sh`; two halves of `format.sh --check`, `style` with `csharpier` and `analyzers`; the `test` matrix, whose four legs each build in `Release` and test with coverage one group of projects on a runner of its own: `tests/SqlSource.Tests`; `tests/SqlSource.Tool.Tests`; the two PostgreSQL projects on the default image; and the two SQL Server projects on the default image with `tests/SqlSource.Repository.Tests`; the tests of `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres` alone again on PostgreSQL 14, and of `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer` alone again on SQL Server 2017, one job each; and `dotnet pack` of the two packages with the three package checks and a `Release` build of the whole solution.  Then `coverage`, the one job that waits for others, merges the legs' coverage into one report.  `tests/SqlSource.Tests.RoslynFloor` is built but its tests run only in `nightly.yml` |
| `publish.yml` | `v*` tags, manual runs on `main` | Calls `build.yml`, pushes the two packages to nuget.org, and for a tag creates a GitHub release and calls `docs.yml` |
| `docs.yml` | Manual runs, called by `publish.yml` for a tag | Builds the manual, `site/`, with `tools/build-site.sh` and deploys it to GitHub Pages, at `https://mbcrawfo.github.io/SqlSource/` |
| `coverage-comment.yml` | A successful `ci.yml` run for a pull request | Posts the coverage report as a comment on the pull request, or updates the comment it posted before |
| `nightly.yml` | Every night, manual runs, pull requests that change the file | Restores, builds in `Release` and runs the tests of every project but `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres`, `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.Npgsql8`, `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer`, `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SqlClient61`, `tests/DatabaseTests/QueryMethodAllocation`, `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.SyncAsync` and `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync` on `windows-latest` and `macos-latest`; and on `ubuntu-latest`, the tests of `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres` on PostgreSQL 15, 16 and 17 and of `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer` on SQL Server 2019 and 2022, one job each, the allocation tests of `tests/DatabaseTests/QueryMethodAllocation` on each engine's default image, `allocation-postgres` and `allocation-sqlserver`, alone and without coverage, and the comparisons of each synchronous method with its asynchronous twin of `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.SyncAsync` and `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync` on each engine's default image, `sync-async-postgres` and `sync-async-sqlserver` |

## The test images

Each floor job of `build.yml` names its floor image once, as `POSTGRES_FLOOR_IMAGE` or `SQLSERVER_FLOOR_IMAGE` of the job's `env`, pulls it in a step of its own, "Pull test image", and runs the tests of one project on it.  Each leg of the matrices `test-postgres` and `test-sqlserver` of `nightly.yml` names its image in its `matrix.include`, pulls it in its own "Pull test image" step and runs the tests of one project on it, the same way.  The step "Pull test images" of the test legs on PostgreSQL and SQL Server of `build.yml`, and that of the two allocation jobs and the two sync-async jobs of `nightly.yml`, run `tools/pull-test-images.sh` after the build and before the first step that runs a test: it pulls the default image of each engine, and the log shows the seconds of each pull, so that the time of a pull is apart from the time of a test.  The pull does not run in the background during the build: tried that way, it saved no time, because it slowed the build by about as long as it took.

Each job that runs a PostGIS test, the test leg on PostgreSQL and `test-postgres-floor` of `build.yml` and `test-postgres` and `sync-async-postgres` of `nightly.yml`, builds the PostGIS image after its pull, in a step of its own, "Build PostGIS image", with the action `.github/actions/postgis-image`, on the image its tests run, and only then runs them.  The action loads the image from the Actions cache, under a key of the image's name, which holds the postgres tag, the PostGIS package and the hash of the Dockerfile; on a miss, or when the cached image fails to load, it builds it with [`tools/build-postgis-image.sh`](../../tools/README.md#building-the-postgis-image) and saves it to the cache at once, so a job whose tests fail still caches it.  A build that fails, as an `apt-get` that cannot reach PostgreSQL's package sources does, fails the job on that step, with Docker's whole output in its log, and no test runs; the tests find the image the step built and build nothing.  The step also keeps the image's ID, from `tools/build-postgis-image.sh --id`, as `POSTGIS_IMAGE_ID`, and a step after the tests, "Check the tests built no PostGIS image", runs `--unchanged` on it whenever the build step succeeded, so that a job whose tests built the image again, which would hide a failed build in their errors once more, fails.

## Artifacts

Each run of `build.yml` uploads two artifacts: `packages`, the two `.nupkg` files, from the `package` job, and `coverage`, from the `coverage` job, the HTML, Cobertura and markdown reports.  Each leg of the `test` matrix uploads the Cobertura files of its projects as `cobertura-<leg>`, whatever their tests' result, and the `coverage` job, which runs unless the run was cancelled, downloads every `cobertura-*` artifact and merges them with ReportGenerator into the report.  The run's job summary also holds the coverage summary and, for each test project a step ran, its counts and its failed and skipped tests.  It lists no passed tests: a step's summary holds 1 MiB, the reporter cuts its output there, and GitHub then shows little or none of that step's summary.  The passed tests of the solution alone are past the limit.

This leaves a limitation of the reporter, which has no option to shorten or cap what it lists: each failed test is listed with its message and stack trace, about 3 KB, so a step where some hundreds of tests fail, as when a project's container does not start, passes 1 MiB again and its summary is lost.  The step's log still holds every failure.

## Continuous integration

The `ci` job succeeds only when every other job in `ci.yml` succeeded or was skipped.  It is the one status check to require in the `main` ruleset.

`coverage-comment.yml` always runs the version on `main`, never the one a pull request changes.  A change to it takes effect, and can first be tried, after it is merged.  A manual run of `publish.yml` on a branch runs the file but skips every job, because its `build` job runs only for a tag or `main`.  A manual run of `docs.yml` builds the branch it is started on, but the `github-pages` environment deploys from `main` and `v*` tags alone, so from any other branch it fails at the deploy.

## Nightly

`ci.yml` runs on Linux alone.  The `roslyn-floor` job of `nightly.yml` runs the tests of `tests/SqlSource.Tests.RoslynFloor` on Linux, which `build.yml` builds but does not test: they are the driver tests of `tests/SqlSource.Tests/Generator/`, which `build.yml` runs on the current Roslyn.  `nightly.yml` is what runs the tests on Windows and macOS, where paths, quoting, exit codes and the kill of a process differ, and what runs the container tests on the supported database majors that `build.yml` does not: PostgreSQL 15, 16 and 17 and SQL Server 2019 and 2022, on Linux, and the only workflow that runs the allocation tests of `tests/DatabaseTests/QueryMethodAllocation`: its jobs `allocation-postgres` and `allocation-sqlserver` each run one engine's, on the default image, without coverage, which allocates in the process they measure, and a red one says a generated method may allocate more than a hand-written one ([how to read it](../../tests/DatabaseTests/QueryMethodAllocation/README.md)).  It is also the only workflow that runs `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.SyncAsync` and `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync`: its jobs `sync-async-postgres` and `sync-async-sqlserver` each run one engine's comparisons of each synchronous method with its asynchronous twin, on the default image, and a red one says a synchronous method may behave otherwise than its twin (how to read it: [PostgreSQL](../../tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.SyncAsync/README.md), [SQL Server](../../tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync/README.md)).  `build.yml` tests each engine's floor and default, so that the two workflows together test every supported major; [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) holds the rule that keeps them so.  Its Windows and macOS job runs no check that needs Docker, none of `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres`, `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.Npgsql8`, `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer`, `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SqlClient61`, `tests/DatabaseTests/QueryMethodAllocation`, `tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres.SyncAsync` and `tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync`, whose containers its runners cannot start, and packs nothing.  The workflow is no required check: a failure is mended in a pull request of its own.  To try a branch on both systems and every database major before it is merged, start the workflow by hand:

```bash
gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref <branch>
```

GitHub sends the result of a scheduled run to whoever last changed the schedule, and turns the schedule of a public repository off after 60 days without activity in the repository; it is turned on again on the workflow's page under Actions.
